newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures up but gains capped by origin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures up but gains capped by origin.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures stayed firm by Wednesday midsession but further upward movement was stalled by persistent producer selling.
Volume remained razor-thin at 1,719 lots as the market struggled to attract fresh interest after the long Easter break and recent wild volatility.
The morning dealings saw some light activity in May/July and July/Sept switches by the trade.

The market was called up to $150 higher on paper and $75 in practice but May only managed to gap $36 up. The contract then hit the session high of $1,657 a tonne before closing the morning back at its opening level.
New York arabica futures were higher on Tuesday on speculative and local buying but traders detected no new fundamental factors behind the rise.
The U.S. market was called to open 2.00-3.00 cents down in theory.

News that stevedores at Brazil's key port of Santos have gone on a strike on Wednesday over a labour dispute had no immediate impact on the market and traders said it was hard to tell if it might react later.
"I don't think there will be a major impact as coffee shipments are traditionally slow at this time of the year but you can't never say there will be no market impact," said one.

The latest International Coffee Organization (ICO) export data, as expected, showed that coffee exports continued to be front-loaded as Central and South American producers took advantage of the recent price rally to unload their holdings.
As such, growers would have little coffee left to sell before the next crop harvest later this year.
The ICO said its exporting members exports rose to 7.41 million 60-kg bags in February from 6.87 million in January and 6.66 million in February 1996.
In the first five months of the current 1996/97 coffee year to February total exports were up at 34.26 million from 30.30 million in the same 1995/96 period.
